_provenance.method: p05/p95 of studio.style_metrics.measure_frame over 800 frames sampled uniformly at random (seed 11) from the 18,709-frame reference corpus in assets/refs/. Numbers only; no competitor media is committed.
_provenance.why_rebuilt: Every previous band was copied from 04-video-forensics.md, whose numbers our code cannot reproduce. Measured with OUR measure_frame, real reference frames give median saturation 0.234 (research says 0.270), near_white 43.5 (research 29.3) and colour_bins 49 (research 16.2) — the last off by 3x. The research never documents its method, so those numbers were never valid thresholds for this implementation. Run 20260803-113248 was refused by them after paying for research, script and 432s of TTS; measured against THIS envelope the same frames sit comfortably inside.
_provenance.known_limitation: The reference varies enormously frame to frame (saturation p05 0.058 to p95 0.508), so a p05/p95 band is a WIDE gate: it catches catastrophic drift such as photorealistic or dense-colour output, not subtle drift. A stronger gate would compare distributions over many frames rather than the median of three. Honest and weak beats confident and wrong.
_provenance.UNRESOLVED: This envelope is NOT trustworthy and the gate should be treated as advisory. Two reasons. (1) Provenance: assets/refs/frame_*.jpg dates to 2026-07-07 and nothing in this repo generates it, so which video or channel these 18,709 frames come from cannot be verified from the code. (2) Discrimination: per-frame variance is enormous — the same corpus yields colour_bins from 16 to 72 — so a p05/p95 band is wide enough to admit almost anything. measure_frame does not currently capture what 'on-style' means. Calibrating it properly needs a corpus with recorded provenance and a metric validated against it; until then a confident-looking gate is worse than an honest one.
_provenance.colour_bins_ungated: Left OUT of the gated set: 16 vs 72 on frames from one corpus is not a style signal.
